source_text: Quae tamen gratia, quoniam etiam medicina dicitur, salva lege iustitiae facit alios ex malis bonos, parvulos autem, quos creat condendo bonos, reddit innovando adoptandoque meliores.
pass_a_gloss: Which grace nevertheless, since it is also called medicine, with the law of justice saved makes some from evils good, but little ones, whom he creates good by founding, it renders better by renewing and adopting.

lemmas.lexica: LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
LS parvulus; Blaise infants without usus rationis
LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: Yet this grace, because it is also called medicine, makes some people good from being evil, while preserving the law of justice. But infants, whom God makes good by creating them, it makes better by renewing and adopting them.

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: Julian means Scripture's legal/authoritative witness, especially the divine Law as teacher of justice.
rejected: natural law (unless the sentence is philosophical)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: Renewal by baptism recalls the washing of regeneration and renewal.
Adoption by grace recalls the Pauline adoption language.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
